flags.reason: In the filament lamp investigation the filament is meant to heat up (that is why its resistance rises), so 'to stop the filament heating up' is a muddled reason; switching off between readings is to keep a fixed resistor (and the wires) from warming and changing resistance.
flags.fix: Reword to 'In the resistor practical, why should the circuit be switched off between readings?' Answer: To stop the resistor heating up. Accept: Keep its temperature constant; so its resistance stays the same.
